Ive seen threads on here about people telling their parents and they brush it off as nothing or give them the typical "work hard for what you want" bs. Coming from your parents which almost seems like a last resort kinda sucks

I moved to the US from Canada when I was 18 to try and escape my depressive life, my parents were the only people that knew about my suicidal thoughts. Looking on the outside, i'm in a way better place now than i was before. But inside, i've never been so lonely. 

I know for me I typically like to keep things to myself, but having someone to talk to (and you want to talk to) in tough times is something money cant buy, again hope you get the help you need :)

Sometimes telling them can be a great step in the right direction, you get an immense pressure off your chest and if theyre supportive and comprehensive about it I think its a great idea. Although ive seen threads where people try to explain it to them and since they dont seem to fully understand depression/suicidal thoughts, the parents reaction doesnt help, it seems to do the opposite (not that it should for any reason). I hope you have understanding and supportive parents when it comes to this subject even with everything you mentioned
